code: library(mlr3) logit_ = function(y, x, start = NULL, weights = NULL, offset = NULL, ...) {   glm(y ~ 1, family = binomial, start = start, ...) } learner = LearnerClassifMob$new() learner$param_set$values$rhs = "." learner$param_set$values$fit = logit_ learner$param_set$values$additional = list(maxit = 100) learner$feature_types = c("logical", "integer", "numeric", "factor", "ordered") learner$properties = c("twoclass", "weights")  predict_fun = function(object, newdata, task, .type) {   p = unname(predict(object, newdata = newdata, type = "response"))   levs = task$levels(task$target_names)[[1L]]    if (.type == "response") {     ifelse(p < 0.5, levs[1L], levs[2L])   } else {     y = matrix(c(1 - p, p), ncol = 2L, nrow = length(p))     colnames(y) = levs     y   } } task = tsk("breast_cancer") learner$param_set$values$predict_fun = predict_fun ids = partition(task) learner$train(task, row_ids = ids$train) learner$predict(task, row_ids = ids$test) #>  #> ── <PredictionClassif> for 225 observations: ─────────────────────────────────── #>  row_ids     truth  response #>        2    benign malignant #>        4    benign malignant #>        7    benign    benign #>      ---       ---       --- #>      662    benign malignant #>      665 malignant malignant #>      668    benign malignant

Blocks sorted increasing penalty factor, .e., blocks larger MAC (stronger average signal) receive higher priority (come first). Also, block‑wise penalty factors attached fitted model object learner$model$block.penalty.factors. method useful domain knowledge available specify block priority. step, data standardized default (standardize = TRUE), can overridden learner's standardize parameter. lambda.min always used derive block priority. text: adaptive.order: TRUE, priority order blocks estimated data following Herrmann et al. (2021), instead using user-supplied block order. block, Ridge regression (alpha = 0) fit using cv.glmnet() block alone. importance block measured mean absolute coefficient (MAC) score lambda.min value (lambda giving minimum cross-validation error). penalty factor 1 / MAC assigned block. Blocks sorted increasing penalty factor, .e., blocks larger MAC (stronger average signal) receive higher priority (come first). Also, block‑wise penalty factors attached fitted model object learner$model$block.penalty.factors. method useful domain knowledge available specify block priority. step, data standardized default (standardize = TRUE), can overridden learner's standardize parameter. lambda.min always used derive block priority. Additional arguments nfolds, type.measure, weights cox.ties (provided) forwarded block‑wise cv.glmnet() fit. max.coef parameter, supplied, re‑ordered accordingly align new block order. parameter ignored fewer two blocks provided. defaults FALSE backward compatibility.

code: # Simulate regression data set.seed(1L) x = matrix(rnorm(50L * 500L), nrow = 50L, ncol = 500L) data = as.data.frame(x) data$y = rnorm(50L)  # Define a Task task = mlr3::as_task_regr(data, target = "y")  # Create train and test set ids = partition(task)  # Define the Learner and set parameter values learner = lrn("regr.priority_lasso",   blocks = list(bp1 = 1:75, bp2 = 76:200, bp3 = 201:500),   max.coef = c(Inf, 8, 5),   block1.penalization = TRUE,   lambda.type = "lambda.min",   standardize = TRUE,   nfolds = 5,   cvoffset = FALSE)  # Train the learner on the training ids learner$train(task, row_ids = ids$train)  # Selected features learner$selected_features() #> [1] "V424" "V440"  # Make predictions for the test rows predictions = learner$predict(task, row_ids = ids$test)  # Score the predictions predictions$score() #>  regr.mse  #> 0.3961006

title: SurvDNN Survival Learner — mlr_learners_surv.survdnn
text: Deep neural network survival models package survdnn, aimed tabular (low moderate-dimensional) covariate settings using torch-based multilayer perceptrons. learner wraps survdnn::survdnn().

title: SurvDNN Survival Learner — mlr_learners_surv.survdnn
text: learner supports following prediction types: lp numeric vector linear predictors, one per observation. loss "cox" / "cox_l2" log-risk score (higher implies worse prognosis). "aft", predict.survdnn() returns predicted log-time location \(\mu(x)\) (higher implies better prognosis), therefore learner internally negates higher values imply higher risk (consistent mlr3 conventions). "coxtime", \(g(t_0, x)\) evaluated reference time. crank lp. distr survival matrix (rows = observations, columns = time points) based predict(type = "survival"). default, predictions evaluated unique event times training data.

title: mlr3extralearners (development version)
text: classif.liblinear regr.liblinear: added regularizeBias parameter LiblineaR::LiblineaR(), available LiblineaR 2.50-1 . classif.rpf regr.rpf: re-added random planted forest learners randomPlantedForest (>= 0.5.0), now supports marshaling can therefore used encapsulation, parallelization, saved disk (#615). Registering learner whose id class name already use now throws error instead silently overwriting existing learner (#614). classif.glmer: added disp_method, maxPhiIter, disp_dof_correction parameters lme4::glmerControl(), available lme4 2.1.0 . regr.botorch_fullybayesian, regr.botorch_mixedsingletaskgp, regr.botorch_singletaskgp: fixed segfaults training prediction R uses recent OpenBLAS (e.g. Ubuntu 26.04), whose cblas_dgemm_batch() called torch instead MKL version. torch now imported RTLD_DEEPBIND imported . data also copied torch tensors instead sharing read-memory R matrix. regr.glm: added tol wtol parameters stats::glm.control(), available R 4.7.0 . Update CoxBoost version 1.5.2 fixes prediction CIF bug enabling prediction one observation time point upstream package (need handle mlr3 side). Use mlr3cmprsk version 0.0.6.

title: mlr3extralearners 1.7.0
text: surv.cv_glmnet surv.glmnet: added strata parameter fitting stratified Cox models via glmnet::stratifySurv() (#396).

text: classif.mlp renamed classif.mlp_rsnns id clashed classif.mlp learner mlr3torch.

title: mlr3extralearners 1.7.0
text: classif.catboost regr.catboost now report $internal_valid_scores, previously always empty, eval_metric loss_function. classif.catboost, regr.catboost, classif.lightgbm, regr.lightgbm, surv.xgboost.aft surv.xgboost.cox gained $best_valid_scores field, msr("best_valid_score") can used . fix: classif.lightgbm regr.lightgbm reported $internal_valid_scores last boosting iteration, although LightGBM predicts model$best_iter. scores now taken model$best_iter therefore describe model used prediction. New learners classif.tabfm regr.tabfm interfacing tabfm Python package, tabular foundation model Google Research. classif.tabpfn regr.tabpfn: added support feature types character, factor, ordered, encoded categorical features tabpfn. level order ordered features preserved. Previously features converted numeric matrix, ruled categorical features even though tabpfn supports . New learners classif.bam regr.bam fitting fast generalized additive models large datasets mgcv::bam() (#355). New learner classif.opls fitting orthogonal partial least squares discriminant analysis ropls::opls() Bioconductor package ropls (#268). New learner regr.grf fitting generalized random forest grf::regression_forest(), supporting se predictions, observation weights, missing feature values. New learner regr.polynomial fitting polynomial regression stats::lm() stats::poly() (#420). classif.tabpfn regr.tabpfn: updated parameter sets match tabpfn 8.1.0, adding auto_scale_n_estimators, keep_cache_on_device, n_preprocessing_jobs, differentiable_input, show_progress_bar (plus eval_metric tuning_config classification), adding "batched" option fit_mode, correcting informational default n_estimators 8. Fixed partial argument-matching bug survival glmnet learners stype matched predict argument s, causing s overwritten stype = 1 2 predictions -regularized.

title: mlr3extralearners 1.6.0
text: Updated minimum versions suggested packages, notably glmnet (>= 5.0) (#594). classif.fastai now pins fastcore Python dependency version 2.0.0 fastai (<= 2.8.7) incompatible fastcore 2.0 declare upper bound. h2o learners longer emit spurious warning outdated H2O cluster version training predicting. surv.cv_glmnet surv.glmnet: updated glmnet v5.0, added train parameters cox.ties (initialized "breslow" keep previous tie-handling behavior), maxp, path, added predict parameter exact (surv.cv_glmnet ), fixed predictions relaxed fits (relax = TRUE), added read-native_model field returns fitted glmnet model (#594). surv.priority_lasso: added train parameter cox.ties, initialized "breslow" (#594). surv.survdnn: added .threads train parameter (#594). regr.botorch_fullybayesian now declares numpyro, jax, jaxlib Python dependencies installed automatically. regr.bart’s hyperparameter sigdf changed type double. regr.crs: added train parameter max.eval compatibility crs (>= 0.15-45) (#601).
